inline_comments.comment: `configApi.getConfig()` is called directly inside `genColor`, and again independently inside `getStyles` (line 31). No other diagram `styles.js` in the codebase does this — the `getStyles` function is meant to be a pure function of its `options` argument, whose values already come from the theme system. `look` and `requirementEdgeLabelBackground` should either be injected into the `options` object before calling `getStyles`, or passed as explicit additional parameters, rather than pulling them from global config inside the styles module. Calling `getConfig()` twice per render (once in each helper) also means two independent global reads when one would suffice.

`bkgColorArray[i]` is accessed without a length guard. The loop runs `options.THEME_COLOR_LIMIT` times, but `bkgColorArray` may be shorter than that. When `i >= bkgColorArray.length`, `bkgColorArray[i]` is `undefined`, which renders as the literal string `"undefined"` in the CSS. Add a bounds check: `bkgColorArray?.length > i ? bkgColorArray[i] : ''`.

The `.edgeLabel` rule is indented 4 spaces, but every surrounding rule (`.reqBox`, `.relationshipLine`, `.divider`, etc.) uses 2 spaces. This indentation mismatch was introduced when the template literal was converted to a function. Align it with the surrounding rules.

`getConfig()` is called directly inside this shape-rendering function. The project rule is that shape rendering functions must not call `getConfig()` directly; they must instead accept a third parameter of type `ShapeRenderOptions` (from `../../types.js`) that carries `config`, and read `themeVariables` from there. Calling `getConfig()` inside a shape blocks the parallel-rendering work the project is actively working toward. Update the function signature to `requirementBox<T>(parent, node, { config }: ShapeRenderOptions)` and derive `themeVariables` from the passed `config`.

`const thickness = 0.001` is a magic number whose purpose (forcing `rc.polygon` to render a visually clean, zero-jitter line rather than a roughjs squiggle) is not obvious to a reader. Extract it to a named constant at the top of the file or function, e.g. `const NEO_DIVIDER_THICKNESS = 0.001`, with a brief comment explaining the technique.

The divider line previously had `dividerLine.attr('style', nodeStyles)` applied so that user-defined styles (e.g. `style req stroke:blue`) propagated to the divider. The new code only applies `.attr('class', 'divider')`, dropping `nodeStyles` entirely for **both** classic and neo looks. In the classic look this is a regression: the `.divider` CSS class uses `options.nodeBorder` regardless of user overrides. If the intent is to normalize the divider to always use the theme border color, document that in a comment; otherwise reapply `nodeStyles` for the classic branch.

The condition `requirementEdgeLabelBackground || borderColorArray?.length` mixes two unrelated predicates (a background color for edge labels, and the presence of a color palette for border cycling) to decide whether to push `nodeStyles` onto roughjs paths. This is hard to follow. Since `requirementEdgeLabelBackground` is only set in redux/redux-dark themes and `borderColorArray` only in neo/redux themes, the actual intent is 'apply roughjs path styles only for neo/redux themes.' Consider deriving an explicit `isNeoOrRedux` boolean or moving this logic under a more readable condition.

`configApi.getConfig()` is called directly inside `requirement_arrow_neo`, which lives in `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/`. The project rule requires that internal rendering utilities in this package must not call `getConfig()` directly; `strokeWidth` (and any other theme value) should be threaded in from the caller that already holds the config. The same issue applies to `requirement_contains_neo` (line 470). Consider accepting a `config` parameter in both functions and updating `insertMarkers` to pass it through.

`stroke-width` is set as a presentation attribute on the `<marker>` element itself rather than on the child `<path>`. SVG presentation attributes do inherit, but setting it on `<marker>` (a non-graphical container element) rather than directly on the path is less reliable across browsers. Compare with `requirement_contains_neo` (line 490), which correctly propagates stroke-width to all children via `.selectAll('*').attr('stroke-width', ...)`. Apply the same approach here: set `stroke-width` directly on the `<path>` element.

A `viewBox='0 0 25 20'` is added to `requirement_arrow_neo` but not to `requirement_arrow` or `requirement_contains_neo`. With `markerUnits='userSpaceOnUse'` and `markerWidth=20`, this viewBox introduces an X-scale factor of 20/25 = 0.8 mapping the marker's internal coordinates to user space. The path endpoint at `(20, 10)` in viewBox coordinates maps to `(16, 10)` in user space, but `refX=20` is declared in the viewBox coordinate system as the anchor — the arrow tip will be 4 user-space units behind the edge endpoint. Either remove the `viewBox` (the path fits within 20×20 without it) or adjust `refX` and `markerWidth` to be consistent with the viewBox.

The 'should render all relationship types' test builds its diagram string by appending `\n`-escaped strings to `diagram`. The project convention is to write multi-line diagram strings as template literals with real newlines, not `+=` concatenation with embedded `\n` characters. Rewrite this block as a single template literal with proper indentation.

general_comments.comment: `getConfig()` is independently called in `genColor`, `getStyles` (styles.js), `requirementBox` (shapes/requirementBox.ts), and both new marker functions (markers.js). The project's established pattern is that rendering utilities in `rendering-util/` receive config via parameters (through `ShapeRenderOptions` for shapes, or as explicit arguments for helpers), and that styles functions are pure functions of their `options` argument. All four call sites should be refactored: (1) `getStyles`/`genColor` should receive `look` and any extra theme keys through the `options` object; (2) `requirementBox` should accept a `ShapeRenderOptions` third parameter; (3) the two neo marker functions should accept a `config` parameter threaded from `insertMarkers`.

The `genColor` function captures `look` from `getConfig()` at call time and hard-codes it into the generated CSS selector strings (e.g., `[data-look="${look}"]`). If styles happen to be generated before the config look is set, or if the generated CSS is shared across diagrams with different looks in the same page render, the selectors would silently mis-target nodes. Passing `look` explicitly via `options` (rather than fetching it from global config inside the function) would make the data-flow explicit and avoid this latent issue.

The `requirement_arrow_neo` and `requirement_contains_neo` functions share most of their structure with their non-neo counterparts (`requirement_arrow`, `requirement_contains`) but duplicate all the `append('defs').append('marker').attr(...)` boilerplate. A small factory helper that accepts stroke-width and other neo-specific knobs would reduce duplication and make future look-related changes easier to apply consistently.
